title: Company data areas and shared records
question: Where should you start an investigation, and which records are shared?
alt: Nine data areas organize all 82 tables. Sales, Design Services, purchasing, manufacturing, payroll, accounting, fixed assets, planning, and shared master records have focused linked views. The layout groups evidence rather than imposing a company-wide sequence.
boundary: These are learning areas, not additional database tables or proof of departmental independence.

title: Accounts, journals, and posted detail
question: Which source identifier identifies the posted event?

relationships.note: Other posting types have their own source records.

boundary: JournalEntry is one posting route. Operational sources and constructed PayrollSummary identifiers must not be treated as journal headers.

tables.name: GLEntry
tables.grain: One posted account line in a voucher

alt: Accounts, journals, and posted detail. Which source identifier identifies the posted event? Primary tables: Account, JournalEntry, GLEntry. JournalEntry is one posting route. Operational sources and constructed PayrollSummary identifiers must not be treated as journal headers.

title: Asset events and financing
question: Which asset event or debt installment links to a journal?
boundary: Asset and debt records link to journals when present; they do not post under their own GLEntry source labels.

tables.name: FixedAsset
tables.grain: One asset in the asset register

alt: Asset events and financing. Which asset event or debt installment links to a journal? Primary tables: FixedAsset, FixedAssetEvent, DebtAgreement, DebtScheduleLine. Asset and debt records link to journals when present; they do not post under their own GLEntry source labels.

title: Customer orders and commercial terms
question: Which terms describe an order without recognizing revenue?
boundary: Segment price lists need no CustomerID. A linked approval records an authorization basis; inspect authority, dates, and status separately.

tables.name: PriceList
tables.grain: One customer or segment price-list scope

tables.name: PriceListLine
tables.grain: One item price within a price list

tables.name: SalesOrderLine
tables.grain: One ordered item or service line

alt: Customer orders and commercial terms. Which terms describe an order without recognizing revenue? Primary tables: Customer, PriceList, PriceListLine, PromotionProgram, PriceOverrideApproval, SalesOrder, SalesOrderLine. Segment price lists need no CustomerID. A linked approval records an authorization basis; inspect authority, dates, and status separately.

title: Goods fulfillment and customer billing
question: Which line-level keys connect ordered, shipped, and billed quantities?
boundary: ShipmentLineID is optional on customer invoice lines because services use ServiceBillingLine. This view focuses on the goods path; an order is non-posting.

tables.name: SalesInvoiceLine
tables.grain: One billed goods or service line

tables.name: SalesOrderLine
tables.grain: One ordered item or service line

alt: Goods fulfillment and customer billing. Which line-level keys connect ordered, shipped, and billed quantities? Primary tables: Shipment, ShipmentLine, SalesInvoice, SalesInvoiceLine. ShipmentLineID is optional on customer invoice lines because services use ServiceBillingLine. This view focuses on the goods path; an order is non-posting.

title: Design work, time, and billing
question: How are dated time entries matched to a billing-period rollup?

relationships.note: Match engagement; WorkDate lies within BillingPeriodStartDate and BillingPeriodEndDate. Aggregate approved billable hours before comparing.

boundary: The time-to-billing match is an engagement/date-interval analysis, not a stored billing-line ID on each time entry. Non-billable time retains cost support without customer billing.

tables.name: ServiceEngagement
tables.grain: One engagement for a service order line

tables.name: ServiceEngagementAssignment
tables.grain: One employee assignment to an engagement

tables.name: ServiceTimeEntry
tables.grain: One employee service-time entry on a work date

tables.name: ServiceBillingLine
tables.grain: One engagement billing-period rollup linked to an invoice line

tables.name: SalesOrderLine
tables.grain: One ordered item or service line

tables.name: SalesInvoiceLine
tables.grain: One billed goods or service line

alt: Design work, time, and billing. How are dated time entries matched to a billing-period rollup? Primary tables: ServiceEngagement, ServiceEngagementAssignment, ServiceTimeEntry, ServiceBillingLine. The time-to-billing match is an engagement/date-interval analysis, not a stored billing-line ID on each time entry. Non-billable time retains cost support without customer billing.

title: Received cash and invoice allocation
question: Why can received cash and an open invoice coexist?
boundary: Receipt and invoice dates do not establish allocation. CashReceiptApplication supplies the amount and application date; CashReceipt.SalesInvoiceID is compatibility metadata.

tables.name: CashReceiptApplication
tables.grain: One dated receipt allocation to an invoice

alt: Received cash and invoice allocation. Why can received cash and an open invoice coexist? Primary tables: CashReceipt, CashReceiptApplication. Receipt and invoice dates do not establish allocation. CashReceiptApplication supplies the amount and application date; CashReceipt.SalesInvoiceID is compatibility metadata.

title: Returns, customer credit, and refunds
question: Which records distinguish returned goods, credit, and cash paid back?
boundary: A memo can reduce AR and retain excess customer credit. A refund is a separate optional cash event; do not infer one from a return.

tables.name: CustomerRefund
tables.grain: One cash refund against a credit memo

alt: Returns, customer credit, and refunds. Which records distinguish returned goods, credit, and cash paid back? Primary tables: SalesReturn, SalesReturnLine, CreditMemo, CreditMemoLine, CustomerRefund. A memo can reduce AR and retain excess customer credit. A refund is a separate optional cash event; do not infer one from a return.

title: Commission accrual, clawback, and payment
question: How does a payment identify its accruals and adjustments?
boundary: The accrual stores both the invoice-line and rate keys. Payment lines use a type-qualified source ID; commissions settle separately from payroll.

tables.name: SalesCommissionRate
tables.grain: One commission rate by revenue type, segment, and effective period

tables.name: SalesCommissionPaymentLine
tables.grain: One accrual or adjustment included in a commission payment

tables.name: SalesInvoiceLine
tables.grain: One billed goods or service line

alt: Commission accrual, clawback, and payment. How does a payment identify its accruals and adjustments? Primary tables: SalesCommissionRate, SalesCommissionAccrual, SalesCommissionAdjustment, SalesCommissionPayment, SalesCommissionPaymentLine. The accrual stores both the invoice-line and rate keys. Payment lines use a type-qualified source ID; commissions settle separately from payroll.

title: Procurement and goods receiving
question: Which requisition and PO line support a received quantity?
boundary: Use PurchaseOrderLine.RequisitionID for a batched order. A stored receipt/invoice relationship does not prove a system-enforced matching control.
alt: Procurement and goods receiving. Which requisition and PO line support a received quantity? Primary tables: Supplier, PurchaseRequisition, PurchaseOrder, PurchaseOrderLine, GoodsReceipt, GoodsReceiptLine. Use PurchaseOrderLine.RequisitionID for a batched order. A stored receipt/invoice relationship does not prove a system-enforced matching control.

title: Supplier invoices and separate settlement
question: Does the supplier line match received goods or an accrued-service estimate?
boundary: GoodsReceiptLineID and POLineID are absent on direct accrued-service invoice lines. Payment clears AP; it does not prove that a residual estimate has cleared.

tables.name: PurchaseInvoiceLine
tables.grain: One goods or accrued-service supplier invoice line

alt: Supplier invoices and separate settlement. Does the supplier line match received goods or an accrued-service estimate? Primary tables: PurchaseInvoice, PurchaseInvoiceLine, DisbursementPayment. GoodsReceiptLineID and POLineID are absent on direct accrued-service invoice lines. Payment clears AP; it does not prove that a residual estimate has cleared.

title: Product recipes and production capacity
question: Which item, component, operation, and work center define production?
boundary: BOM and routing definitions support planned work. Their existence does not establish material issue, completion, or cost close.

tables.name: WorkCenterCalendar
tables.grain: One work center on one calendar date

tables.name: Item
tables.grain: One item in the product or service master

alt: Product recipes and production capacity. Which item, component, operation, and work center define production? Primary tables: BillOfMaterial, BillOfMaterialLine, Routing, RoutingOperation, WorkCenter, WorkCenterCalendar. BOM and routing definitions support planned work. Their existence does not establish material issue, completion, or cost close.

title: Work orders and daily operation schedules
question: Which two fields match a scheduled operation to available daily capacity?

relationships.note: Match BOTH work center and date. Aggregate scheduled operations at work-center/date grain before comparing available hours.

boundary: No WorkCenterCalendarID is stored on the schedule. Joining on work center alone repeats calendar capacity.

tables.name: WorkOrderOperation
tables.grain: One operation within a work order

tables.name: WorkOrderOperationSchedule
tables.grain: One scheduled operation on a work-center date

tables.name: SupplyPlanRecommendation
tables.grain: One item/location supply recommendation in a planning bucket

tables.name: WorkCenterCalendar
tables.grain: One work center on one calendar date

alt: Work orders and daily operation schedules. Which two fields match a scheduled operation to available daily capacity? Primary tables: WorkOrder, WorkOrderOperation, WorkOrderOperationSchedule. No WorkCenterCalendarID is stored on the schedule. Joining on work center alone repeats calendar capacity.

title: Material, completion, and accounting close
question: Which independent branches must be summarized before a work-order comparison?
boundary: Close does not store a ProductionCompletionLineID. Aggregate issues, labor, completions, and close independently. Payroll clearing remains pooled by period/cost center.

tables.name: LaborTimeEntry
tables.grain: One labor allocation supporting an operation and pay period

alt: Material, completion, and accounting close. Which independent branches must be summarized before a work-order comparison? Primary tables: MaterialIssue, MaterialIssueLine, ProductionCompletion, ProductionCompletionLine, WorkOrderClose. Close does not store a ProductionCompletionLineID. Aggregate issues, labor, completions, and close independently. Payroll clearing remains pooled by period/cost center.

title: Attendance support and approved daily time
question: Which stored keys connect a daily time record to its supporting evidence?
boundary: There is no assignment ID on the roster or punch ID on AttendanceException. Effective-date matching and shared roster/time records supply those investigations; a flag does not prove a payment block.

tables.name: EmployeeShiftAssignment
tables.grain: One employee shift assignment over effective dates

tables.name: EmployeeShiftRoster
tables.grain: One employee planned shift on a roster date

tables.name: EmployeeAbsence
tables.grain: One absence record against a roster

tables.name: TimeClockEntry
tables.grain: One approved-time record for an employee work date

alt: Attendance support and approved daily time. Which stored keys connect a daily time record to its supporting evidence? Primary tables: ShiftDefinition, EmployeeShiftAssignment, EmployeeShiftRoster, EmployeeAbsence, OvertimeApproval, TimeClockPunch, TimeClockEntry, AttendanceException. There is no assignment ID on the roster or punch ID on AttendanceException. Effective-date matching and shared roster/time records supply those investigations; a flag does not prove a payment block.

title: Payroll support, employee pay, and remittances
question: Which obligation is employee-specific, and which is period-level?
boundary: PayrollSummary is a constructed GLEntry source label, not a table. Aggregate registers by period, cost center, and account to reconcile recognition; remittances have a different grain from employee payments.

tables.name: LaborTimeEntry

tables.name: PayrollRegister

tables.name: PayrollRegisterLine

alt: Payroll support, employee pay, and remittances. Which obligation is employee-specific, and which is period-level? Primary tables: PayrollPeriod, LaborTimeEntry, PayrollRegister, PayrollRegisterLine, PayrollPayment, PayrollLiabilityRemittance. PayrollSummary is a constructed GLEntry source label, not a table. title: Shared item, warehouse, and employee records
question: Which identifiers let an investigation move across processes?
boundary: These records recur as shared references in process views. Item account mappings, employee approvals, and warehouse context answer different questions; a shared item does not identify one receipt-to-issue transaction.

tables.name: Item
tables.grain: One item in the product or service master

alt: Shared item, warehouse, and employee records. Which identifiers let an investigation move across processes? Primary tables: Item, Warehouse, Employee. These records recur as shared references in process views. Item account mappings, employee approvals, and warehouse context answer different questions; a shared item does not identify one receipt-to-issue transaction.

title: Budgets and reporting responsibility
question: How do detailed budget drivers differ from a cost-center summary?
boundary: Some BudgetLine rows have no CostCenterID. Budget and BudgetLine are separate grains; do not join their amounts as if they were matching individual transactions.

tables.name: BudgetLine
tables.grain: One monthly budget driver or statement-planning detail

alt: Budgets and reporting responsibility. How do detailed budget drivers differ from a cost-center summary? Primary tables: CostCenter, Budget, BudgetLine. Some BudgetLine rows have no CostCenterID. Budget and BudgetLine are separate grains; do not join their amounts as if they were matching individual transactions.

title: Demand, supply recommendations, and requirements
question: Which links are stored, and which are analytical planning context?

relationships.note: Match item/location and the relevant weekly bucket and DriverType; there is no stored DemandForecastID.
Inspect item/location, active policy, planning bucket, and DriverType; there is no stored InventoryPolicyID.

boundary: Planning context is not a one-record foreign-key trace. Requisitions and work orders reference SupplyPlanRecommendationID when converted into execution documents.

tables.name: DemandForecast
tables.grain: One item/location forecast for a weekly bucket

tables.name: SupplyPlanRecommendation
tables.grain: One item/location supply recommendation in a planning bucket

tables.name: MaterialRequirementPlan
tables.grain: One component requirement for a supply recommendation

tables.name: RoughCutCapacityPlan
tables.grain: One work-center capacity requirement for a supply recommendation

alt: Demand, supply recommendations, and requirements. Which links are stored, and which are analytical planning context? Primary tables: DemandForecast, InventoryPolicy, SupplyPlanRecommendation, MaterialRequirementPlan, RoughCutCapacityPlan. Planning context is not a one-record foreign-key trace.
